item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-b2075922d0dcd57d","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Le 20 septembre 2023, Tshisekedi a annoncé l’accélération du retrait progressif de la MONUSCO à partir de décembre 2023, en affirmant que la RDC devait devenir le principal acteur de sa propre stabilité; il a aussi demandé des sanctions contre les auteurs de crimes graves et refusé le dialogue avec le M23 tant qu’il ne respecterait pas les engagements de paix.","question_ids":["2B.7","2B.9","2B.10","8B.1","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023 decisions and stated crisis policy.","ruler_attribution":"Presidential speech reported by the Presidency.","limitations":["The source reports decisions and rhetoric, not their subsequent implementation or effects."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b2075922d0dcd57d","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Tshisekedi confirmed that general elections would be held in December 2023 and stated that measures were being taken for transparency, inclusiveness, equal opportunity, credibility, and international and NGO observation missions.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.10","8B.1","8B.2"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly concerns the 2023 electoral process.","ruler_attribution":"Presidential announcement reported by the Presidency.","limitations":["The passage describes planned safeguards and invitations, not verified election quality or acceptance of results."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1f1757b331126727","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"In his 14 November 2023 address to Parliament, Tshisekedi reported reforms intended to strengthen the army’s response and deterrence capacities and reiterated the necessity of MONUSCO’s departure.","question_ids":["2B.8","8B.1","8B.2","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns the ruler’s reported 2023 security policy.","ruler_attribution":"Annual state-of-the-nation address reported by the Presidency.","limitations":["The source gives no budget, implementation record, or independent assessment of the military reforms."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1f1757b331126727","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Tshisekedi stated that economic growth had risen from 1.7% in 2020 to 6.2% in 2023 and announced targeted interventions on essential-food prices and monetary policies to stabilize the Congolese franc.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.9","5B.10"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The reported outcome and announced measures include 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Annual state-of-the-nation address reported by the Presidency.","limitations":["The growth claim is a presidential assertion in a self-reported bilan; the passage does not establish causal attribution or implementation results for the anti-inflation measures."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1f1757b331126727","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"To support free primary education, the government reportedly increased the education budget by 9.1% from 2021 to 2022 and by 23.9% from 2022 to 2023; the reported average teacher salary rose from 159,662.67 FC to 408,689.67 FC during the quinquennium.","question_ids":["6B.1","6B.2","6B.4","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Includes a 2023 budget change and cumulative first-term figures.","ruler_attribution":"Figures presented by Tshisekedi in his annual address.","limitations":["The source does not independently verify service quality, access, distribution, or whether budget execution matched allocations."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1f1757b331126727","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Tshisekedi claimed that the DRC had risen 30 places in Reporters Without Borders’ global press-freedom barometer over four years, while calling for greater responsibility and professionalism from journalists during security coverage and the election campaign.","question_ids":["4B.3","4B.6","4B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The claimed change spans the period ending in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Presidential statement reported by the Presidency.","limitations":["The source does not provide the underlying RSF scores or assess government restrictions and enforcement independently."]},{"source_id":"SRC-bc8049d72934bbd3","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The Presidency’s duplicate 14 November 2023 report repeats that the government increased education funding by 9.1% from 2021 to 2022 and 23.9% from 2022 to 2023, while average teacher salary rose from 159,662.67 FC to 408,689.67 FC during the first term.","question_ids":["6B.1","6B.2","6B.4","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Includes a 2023 budget change and cumulative first-term figures.","ruler_attribution":"Presidential address reported by the Presidency.","limitations":["This is a duplicate publication of the same reported claim and does not independently corroborate it."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a96c66663730a20f","start_unit":1,"end_unit":1,"fact_summary":"Execution data presented to Parliament for 2023 showed central-government revenues at 91.22% of forecast, general-budget execution at 87.38%, and central-government expenditure at 96.49% of forecast; end-period inflation was 33.9% and annual-average inflation 23.33%.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.7","5B.9","5B.10","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly reports 2023 fiscal execution and inflation.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the figures to Finance Minister Doudou Fwamba Likunde Li-botayi; it does not establish personal presidential direction.","limitations":["The source reports aggregate execution and macroeconomic outcomes, not whether Tshisekedi personally selected or corrected the policies."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2644ef4dd929843a","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"On 17 April 2023, about 70 Kisangani war victims staging sit-ins before the Prime Minister’s office reportedly experienced violence, humiliation, beatings, theft, and abduction by national police officers; they were seeking unpaid compensation promised after Tshisekedi took office and information about $65 million paid by Uganda in 2022 under an ICJ judgment.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.8","3B.9","6B.3","6B.7","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns an alleged police incident and unresolved compensation claims in April 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the allegations to human-rights organizations and a victims’ movement; it does not establish Tshisekedi’s direct order or response.","limitations":["The allegations are reported claims, not a judicial finding in the supplied text."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b3ec5f9f327f58d5","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"For the 2023–2024 school year, UNICEF reported that nearly 27 million children were already enrolled and nearly 7 million were out of school; more than 800,000 children had been displaced since the beginning of 2023 and more than 2,000 schools had closed in eastern provinces because of insecurity and displacement.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.9","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","6B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly reports conditions during the 2023 school-year opening.","ruler_attribution":"UNICEF reports the conditions and describes collaboration with the education ministry and authorities; direct presidential responsibility is not established.","limitations":["The source does not quantify Tshisekedi’s own funding, orders, or corrective actions."]},{"source_id":"SRC-13deaef6149be7d2","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"FAO’s 2023 humanitarian listings described the DRC as the world’s largest food crisis, with one in four people facing acute hunger, and identified conflict, displacement, and other humanitarian pressures in 2023.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.9","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","6B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The listing includes the 2023 Humanitarian Response Plan and 2023 monitoring publications.","ruler_attribution":"FAO reports national conditions; the supplied page does not attribute them to Tshisekedi’s decisions.","limitations":["This is a publication index and provides no detailed evidence of presidential policy or implementation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e2ee7663ff6a79e7","start_unit":4,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"In May 2023, the UN reported allegations of conflict-related sexual violence by armed men against women and girls in IDP camps around Goma; UNICEF had recorded more than 38,000 GBV cases in North Kivu during 2022, and humanitarian actors assisted over 600 survivors in six camps over two weeks. Many survivors could not access post-exposure prophylaxis within 72 hours.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.7","3B.9","6B.3","6B.6","6B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns conditions and protection needs reported in May 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The UN called on the government to secure IDP camps and prosecute perpetrators; the passage does not show Tshisekedi’s specific response.","limitations":["The reported acts are allegations and the source does not establish presidential authorization or personal involvement."]},{"source_id":"SRC-609293e6a90cb072","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"On 29 September 2023, FAO and WFP reported that more than 25 million people in the DRC faced crisis or emergency food insecurity, over 5.6 million were displaced in Ituri, North Kivu, and South Kivu, and conflict and insufficient rural investment were disrupting agriculture and infrastructure. WFP faced a $629.6 million six-month funding shortfall.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.9","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","6B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly reports national humanitarian conditions in September 2023.","ruler_attribution":"FAO and WFP attribute causes to conflict, infrastructure and investment deficits, and humanitarian funding constraints; personal presidential responsibility is not established.","limitations":["The source does not identify which share of the conditions resulted from Tshisekedi’s policies or authority."]},{"source_id":"SRC-7d183ffcc155044b","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"On 19 October 2023, Goma youth organizations held a peaceful march criticizing the perceived passivity of the EAC force in the M23 war; police reportedly escorted the march, and EAC officials received the protesters’ memorandum and said it would be transmitted to the political level.","question_ids":["2B.6","2B.7","3B.8","4B.3","4B.10","8B.9"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly concerns a peaceful protest and official handling in October 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report describes police conduct and EAC officials’ response; it does not establish a direct Tshisekedi order.","limitations":["The source does not show whether the protest’s demands affected national policy or whether similar protests were consistently handled peacefully."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-993a6ef6d0ed999c","SRC-7fa753edf6309c3d"],"batch_limitations":["The supplied corpus is uneven: several sources are official self-reports or publication indexes, while many adverse facts concern conditions without establishing direct presidential causation.","Duplicate Presidency reports were retained only where the duplicate document itself supplied the same material fact; the duplication is noted as a limitation rather than treated as independent corroboration."]}
